conventions.convention: All tensor products are algebraic over a field; Sweedler expressions denote finite sums.
Quasi-coassociativity is (id⊗Δ)Δ(h)=Φ(Δ⊗id)Δ(h)Φ⁻¹. The associator acts by Φ from left-parenthesized to right-parenthesized tensors; normalization is (id⊗ε⊗id)(Φ)=1⊗1.
A quasi-antipode has a unital algebra antihomomorphism S; a quasi-Hopf algebra additionally requires S bijective. Ordinary Hopf antipodes and weak Hopf antipodes are not required to be bijective.
The counital maps are ε_t(h)=Σ ε(1_(1)h)1_(2), ε_s(h)=Σ 1_(1)ε(h1_(2)), and ε_s′(h)=Σ 1_(1)ε(1_(2)h). Their multiplication orders are fixed.
For left H-modules the balancing base is H_t, with right action v◁x=ε_s′(x)v and left action on the second factor by restriction. The tensor unit is H_t with h·x=ε_t(hx).
The C2 example is over ℂ, with addition modulo 2, ω(a,b,c)=(-1)^(abc), α=p_0-p_1, β=1, and S=id. Its stated conclusion distinguishes Φ≠1 from a claim about twist equivalence.

load_bearing.statement: A weak bialgebra is an associative unital algebra and coassociative counital coalgebra with multiplicative coproduct, satisfying the displayed weak-unit and weak-counit identities. The definition fixes ε_t, ε_s and ε_s′. A weak Hopf algebra additionally has S satisfying the three displayed antipode identities, without a bijectivity requirement.

For a weak bialgebra over a field, H_t and H_s are commuting unital subalgebras; ε_t|H_s and ε_s′|H_t are inverse algebra anti-isomorphisms. The element e=(ε_t⊗id)Δ(1) is a separability idempotent for H_t, has the two stated ε-reconstruction identities, and satisfies Δ(1)=Σ ε_s′(e¹)⊗e². For h∈H and x∈H_t, Σ ε_t(h_(1)x)h_(2)=hx and Σ ε_s′(ε_t(h_(2)x))h_(1)=hε_s′(x).

A quasi-bialgebra over a field has unital algebra maps Δ and ε and an invertible Φ satisfying the displayed counit, quasi-coassociativity, pentagon and normalization identities. A quasi-antipode is a triple (S,α,β) satisfying the four displayed identities; a quasi-Hopf algebra requires S bijective.

For a quasi-bialgebra over a field in the stated convention, the category of unital left H-modules is monoidal, with diagonal tensor action, unit k_ε, associator given by Φ acting after canonical rebracketing, and canonical vector-space unit constraints. No quasi-antipode is needed.

For a weak bialgebra over a field and unital left H-modules V,W, with v◁x=ε_s′(x)v, the diagonal action descends to V⊗_(H_t)W. The map [v⊗w]↦Δ(1)·(v⊗w) is a natural isomorphism onto Δ(1)(V⊗_kW). These operations form a monoidal category with rebracketing associator and unit H_t acted on by h·x=ε_t(hx); no antipode is used.

published_dependencies.used_for: Central unital scalar structures, algebra multiplication and algebra homomorphisms.
Field coefficients, algebraic tensor products, finite sums, tensor parentheses and opposite-algebra conventions.
Coassociativity and counitality in the weak-bialgebra definition and ordinary bialgebra boundary.
The ordinary bialgebra special case, the monoid-algebra counterexample and the failure of multiplicative counit in the groupoid example.
Componentwise multiplication and unit in tensor powers of algebras.
Unital module actions and the right H_t-action induced by the counital anti-isomorphism.
H-linearity of tensor maps, associators, unit maps and natural comparison maps.
Descending balanced formulas and determining maps by elementary tensors.
The precise bifunctor, unit, naturality, pentagon and triangle obligations.
Ordinary convolution-inverse antipode equations and the absence of an ordinary bijectivity requirement.
The ordinary antipode is a unital algebra antihomomorphism, as needed for the common quasi-Hopf special case.
Checking the assigned A-page's description of the ordinary coassociative, unital bialgebra module interface.
The scalar convention's permission to suppress parentheses and the underlying vector-space coherence identities.
Canonical tensor-unit maps and their explicit inverses.
The additive balancing presentation and finite elementary-tensor generation underlying the relative-product construction.
